MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](LICENSE)\\n\\nA Linux-only profile switcher for Claude Code. It gives Claude Code an isolated\\n`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` for each account and transparently forwards normal commands\\nto the official Claude executable.\\n\\n```bash\\nclaude account add work\\nclaude account add personal\\nclaude account use work\\nclaude account list\\nclaude account current\\nclaude account remove personal\\n\\nclaude\\nclaude \\\"fix this bug in main.py\\\"\\n```\\n\\nClaude Code itself performs login, logout, credential storage, and token\\nrefresh. `claude-account` never reads or copies credential contents.\\n\\n> [!IMPORTANT]\\n> This is an independent community project. It is not made, endorsed, or\\n> supported by Anthropic. Claude and Claude Code are products of Anthropic.\\n\\n## Requirements\\n\\n- Linux\\n- A working Claude Code installation\\n- Rust 1.85 or later to build from source\\n\\n## Install a release\\n\\nDownload `claude-account-v0.1.1-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz` and its\\n`.sha256` file from the [latest release][releases], then verify and install it:\\n\\n```bash\\nsha256sum --check claude-account-v0.1.1-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz.sha256\\ntar -xzf claude-account-v0.1.1-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz\\n./claude-account install\\n```\\n\\nThe installer prints one `export PATH=...` line. Add that line to `~/.bashrc`\\nand open a new terminal. The shim lives in its own directory; it does not\\nreplace the official Claude executable.\\n\\nConfirm the installation:\\n\\n```bash\\ntype -a claude\\nclaude account list\\n```\\n\\nThe claude-account shim should appear before the official Claude executable.\\n\\n## Build from source\\n\\n```bash\\ngit clone https://github.com/hamzarehmandeveloper/claude-account.git\\ncd claude-account\\ncargo build --locked --release\\n./target/release/claude-account install\\n```\\n\\n## Commands\\n\\n### Add an account\\n\\n```bash\\nclaude account add work\\nclaude account add personal --email you@example.com\\nclaude account add company --sso\\nclaude account add api-billing --console\\n```\\n\\nThis opens Claude Code's official login flow. The first profile becomes active.\\nAdding another profile does not switch the active profile. The command also\\ncompletes Claude Code's local onboarding state, so the next `claude` launch\\nuses the saved login without asking you to authenticate again.\\n\\n### Switch accounts\\n\\n```bash\\nclaude account use work\\n```\\n\\nSwitching affects newly launched Claude processes. Existing sessions keep the\\naccount with which they were started.\\n\\n### Inspect profiles\\n\\n```bash\\nclaude account list\\nclaude account current\\n```\\n\\n`current` prints only the profile name, making it safe to use in scripts.\\n\\n### Remove an account\\n\\n```bash\\nclaude account remove personal\\n```\\n\\nThis runs Claude Code's official `auth logout` inside the profile and\\nunregisters it. Settings and session history are preserved, allowing the same\\nprofile name to reuse them later.\\n\\nTo delete all local data belonging to the profile:\\n\\n```bash\\nclaude account remove personal --purge --yes\\n```\\n\\nRemoving the active profile is refused unless `--force` is supplied.\\n`--purge` permanently deletes that profile's settings, sessions, plugins, and\\nhistory in addition to its stored login.\\n\\n### Get help\\n\\n```bash\\nclaude account --help\\nclaude account add --help\\nclaude account remove --help\\n```\\n\\nAll non-account commands and flags are passed unchanged to the official Claude\\nexecutable:\\n\\n```bash\\nclaude\\nclaude -p \\\"explain this project\\\"\\nclaude --model opus\\nclaude auth status --text\\n```\\n\\n## Storage\\n\\nBy default:\\n\\n```text\\n~/.config/claude-account/state.json\\n~/.local/share/claude-account/profiles/<name>/\\n~/.local/share/claude-account/bin/claude\\n~/.local/share/claude-account/libexec/claude-account\\n```\\n\\nThe standard `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` and `XDG_DATA_HOME` variables are respected.\\n`CLAUDE_ACCOUNT_HOME` can place all application data under one absolute\\ndirectory, which is especially useful for tests.\\n\\nThe state file contains profile names, directory paths, and the real Claude\\nexecutable path. It never contains access or refresh tokens.\\n\\n## Authentication environment variables\\n\\nTo guarantee that the selected profile is actually used, the wrapper removes\\nthese variables from the child Claude process:\\n\\n- `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`\\n- `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`\\n- `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`\\n\\nSet `CLAUDE_ACCOUNT_PRESERVE_AUTH_ENV=1` if you intentionally want those\\nvariables to override profile authentication.\\n\\n## Development\\n\\n```bash\\ncargo fmt --check\\ncargo test --locked --all-targets\\ncargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings\\n```\\n\\nSee [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for the contribution workflow and\\n[SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) for private vulnerability reporting.\\n\\n## License\\n\\nReleased under the [MIT License](LICENSE).\\n\\n[releases]: https://github.com/hamzarehmandeveloper/claude-account/releases\\n\",\n      \"encoding\": \"utf-8\",\n      \"sha\": \"762d02063441dca46b53de5e67723a262ee059d0\",\n      \"display_url\": \"https://github.com/hamzarehmandeveloper/claude-account/blob/main/README.md\",\n      \"display_title\": \"README.md\"\n    },\n    \"isError\": false\n  },\n  \"local\": {\n    \"chunk_id\": \"f59760\",\n    \"wall_time_seconds\": 0.055908375,\n    \"exit_code\": 0,\n    \"original_token_count\": 3647861,\n    \"output\": \"Warning: truncated output (original token count: 3647861)\\n... 13542865 bytes omitted ...\\n\\nshared/locales/es.json:96:  \\\"settings.models.credentialReplaceHint\\\": \\\"Enter a new key to replace the saved one\\\",\\nshared/locales/es.json:101:  \\\"settings.models.provider.codex\\\": \\\"Codex (ChatGPT subscription)\\\",\\nshared/locales/es.json:103:  \\\"settings.models.codex.statusAvailable\\\": \\\"Codex is available via your ChatGPT subscription.\\\",\\nshared/locales/es.json:104:  \\\"settings.models.codex.statusUnavailable\\\": \\\"Codex subscription is not available. ## Codex progress · 2026-07-31T13:59:23.459Z

The project’s central idea is clear: one isolated Claude configuration directory per account, with Claude Code itself owning login and token refresh. OmniHarness already has a richer account-allocation layer, so I’m now checking whether the same isolation boundary exists beneath it or whether credentials are being handled differently.

\"output\": \"# Multi-Account CLI Credentials Design\\n\\n## Goal\\n\\nSupport multiple authentication accounts per coding CLI, let users choose or automate which credentials a worker uses, and track usage/quota per account across subscription and API modes without leaking secrets.\\n\\n## Current State\\n\\n- The Agents settings tab ranks worker types with `WORKER_ALLOWED_TYPES` and `WORKER_DEFAULT_TYPE`.\\n- Runtime startup already accepts one optional `credentialProfile` and resolves profile env through `src/server/agent-runtime/external-credentials.ts`.\\n- `src/server/agent-runtime/manager.ts` applies project-scoped CLI homes for Codex, Claude, Gemini, and OpenCode, but credential profile env is applied after project-scoped storage is chosen.\\n- `accounts` and `credit_events` tables exist, but they are a thin config-backed credit model and are not a complete credential/account source of truth.\\n- `/api/accounts` now returns an explicit redacted DTO through `src/server/accounts/dto.ts`; event snapshots must use the same mapper and must never serialize raw account rows.\\n- Execution events, supervisor interventions, planning review findings, and worker entries now use append-only artifact streams for larger payloads. New account/allocation ledgers should keep hot SQLite rows small and use artifact-backed payloads if details can grow.\\n- Quota recovery is now a durable control-plane workflow built around `recovery_incidents`, `supervisor_scheduled_wakes`, and type-level quota blocking in `src/server/quota/type-blocking.ts`.\\n- Worker availability detects one installation/authentication/quota status per worker type, not per account.\\n- The quota tracking plan explicitly left multi-account as future work. This design makes account id part of quota and allocation from the start.\\n\\n## Readiness Update - 2026-06-29\\n\\nThis design is still directionally correct, but implementation must account for code that landed after the original May 29 draft:\\n\\n- Snapshot account redaction is a hard boundary. Any route or SSE snapshot that carries accounts must return `AccountDto`, not database rows with `authRef`.\\n- Account selection is a conversation/run preference, not only a visual composer detail. It must be carried through `POST /api/conversations`, `POST /api/conversations/:id/messages`, commit/direct conversation flows, and stored on `runs`.\\n- Quota blocking must become account-aware. A quota incident for one Codex account must not block all Codex workers if another healthy Codex account exists.\\n- Worker pool keys must include account-specific credential homes and credential env. Prewarmed workers must never be shared across accounts.\\n- Runtime prewarm must use the same account resolution and env ordering as real spawn.\\n- The legacy `config/accounts.yml`, `CreditManager`, and `CREDIT_STRATEGY=swap_account` surface is still present. Migrate it deliberately instead of assuming it is dead.\\n\\n## Product Shape\\n\\nOmniHarness should treat each usable CLI identity as an account record:\\n\\n- a ChatGPT/Codex subscription login,\\n- a Claude subscription login,\\n- a Gemini OAuth login,\\n- an OpenCode provider login,\\n- an API-key backed account,\\n- an external credential profile,\\n- or a command-backed credential provider.\\n\\nThe user can:\\n\\n- see detected CLIs and detected/default accounts,\\n- add additional accounts for each CLI,\\n- choose a specific account for a run or leave it on Auto,\\n- choose a per-CLI allocation strategy,\\n- see account-level health, identity, quota, usage, cost, last used time, and reset/wait state,\\n- safely set up multiple logins through isolated CLI homes.\\n\\n## Recommended Approach\\n\\nUse a first-class account inventory plus a server-side allocator.\\n\\nAlternative 1, only expanding credential profiles, is too hidden: it can launch workers with different env, but it cannot give the UI good account status, usage, quota, or migration semantics.\\n\\nAlternative 2, only storing account settings JSON, is quick but brittle: it would make allocation, usage, and secrets hard to query/test and would not fit the existing `/api/accounts` and event snapshot model.\\n\\nRecommended: evolve the existing `accounts` concept into real CLI credential accounts, add account allocation/usage tables, and keep legacy settings as migration inputs and fallback compatibility.\\n\\n## Data Model\\n\\nEvolve `accounts` by adding fields rather than deleting the existing table:\\n\\n- `cli_type`: `codex | claude | gemini | opencode`.\\n- `provider`: upstream provider where known, such as `openai`, `anthropic`, `google`, or `opencode`.\\n- `type`: keep as account billing kind, `subscription | api | external`.\\n- `label`: user-facing account name.\\n- `auth_mode`: `local_session | isolated_cli_home | api_key | credential_profile | credential_command | legacy_ref`.\\n- `auth_ref`: non-secret pointer only, such as `setting:ACCOUNT_SECRET_<id>`, `profile:work`, `cli-home:<id>`, or `local-default`.\\n- `enabled`, `priority`, `capacity`, `reset_schedule`.\\n- `status`, `status_checked_at`, `metadata_json`, `created_at`, `updated_at`.\\n\\nAdd:\\n\\n- `account_secrets`: encrypted secret values keyed by account and secret kind. API responses only expose configured/preview metadata.\\n- `worker_credential_allocations`: durable record of `workerId -> accountId`, selected strategy, selection reason, and whether it was explicit or automatic.\\n- `worker_token_usage`: token/cost rows with `accountId`, `workerId`, `workerType`, model, token fields, `costUsd`, and `occurredAt`.\\n- `account_usage_snapshots`: cached read model for quotas, windows, spend, reset times, and source.\\n\\nKeep `credit_events`, but use it as the durable account event ledger for allocation/switch/exhaustion/wait decisions, or rename only in a later migration if needed.\\n\\nKeep account-related SQLite rows queryable and small. If an allocation, usage, or account event needs a large JSON payload, follow the artifact-stream pattern used by `execution_events` and `supervisor_interventions`: store a preview/hash/seq in SQLite and put the body in append-only JSONL.\\n\\nDTO/API rule: database rows are private. All public account payloads, including `/api/accounts`, `/api/events?snapshot=1`, SSE update frames, and runtime-portable route responses, must pass through a whitelist DTO mapper.\\n\\n## Credential Execution\\n\\nIntroduce `src/server/accounts/account-resolver.ts`:\\n\\n- resolves account id to env/unset/metadata,\\n- never returns raw secrets to UI or named events,\\n- supports existing external profile directories and provider commands,\\n- supports account-specific CLI home env before project-scoped storage is applied.\\n\\nImportant runtime change:\\n\\n- resolve account env before `applyProjectScopedCliStorage`,\\n- then let project-scoped storage fill only missing CLI home variables,\\n- then apply account/profile env,\\n- then compute the worker pool key using an account-aware env fingerprint.\\n\\nThis avoids the current single-login bias where project-scoped homes bridge the global Codex/Gemini credentials before account-specific env is known.\\n\\nApply the same ordering in every runtime path, including real spawn and prewarm. `prewarmAgent` must not resolve a different env from `spawnAgent`.\\n\\nAccount-aware pool keys must include at least: `CODEX_HOME`, `CODEX_SQLITE_HOME`, `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, `GEMINI_CLI_HOME`, `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR`, `XDG_DATA_HOME`, `XDG_STATE_HOME`, `XDG_CACHE_HOME`, provider API/token env, `PATH`, and `HOME`.\\n\\nClaude-specific note: the current macOS keychain fallback injects the global Claude OAuth token when no explicit Claude credential env is set. Under account selection, that fallback must only run for `local_session` or a selected account that explicitly allows the global keychain. It must not override or leak into an isolated/account-specific Claude config.\\n\\n## Multiple Login Model\\n\\nFor CLIs that naturally use one global login, additional subscription accounts use isolated CLI homes under app data:\\n\\n- Codex: account sets `CODEX_HOME` and `CODEX_SQLITE_HOME`.\\n- Claude: account sets `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`.\\n- Gemini: account sets `GEMINI_CLI_HOME`.\\n- OpenCode: account sets `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR`, `XDG_DATA_HOME`, `XDG_STATE_HOME`, and `XDG_CACHE_HOME`.\\n\\nThe UI can show a login command for each account, for example `CODEX_HOME=<account-home> codex login`. The app should not delete credential files when an account is removed or disabled; account removal is a DB/settings action unless the user explicitly chooses a separate credential-file cleanup action.\\n\\n## Allocation Strategy\\n\\nCreate `src/server/accounts/account-allocator.ts`.\\n\\nInputs:\\n\\n- worker type,\\n- optional explicit `accountId`,\\n- run/project/model/effort,\\n- configured per-CLI strategy,\\n- current account status/usage/quota,\\n- open quota wait incidents,\\n- active leases/allocations.\\n\\nStrategies:\\n\\n- `manual`: use the selected account only; fail visibly if unavailable.\\n- `priority`: try enabled accounts in priority order.\\n- `round_robin`: spread workers across healthy accounts.\\n- `quota_balanced`: prefer the account with the most remaining usable capacity.\\n- `subscription_then_api`: prefer subscription accounts, spill to API accounts after quota exhaustion.\\n- `wait_for_reset`: pause on the chosen subscription account instead of switching.\\n\\nThe default migration should preserve current behavior as `priority`, with one default account per detected CLI.\\n\\nEvery worker spawn stores the selected account in `worker_credential_allocations`. Resume/recovery should reuse the same account unless the selected strategy explicitly allows a switch after quota exhaustion.\\n\\nQuota blocking changes:\\n\\n- replace type-only blocking (`codex` blocked) with account-aware blocking (`codex/account-a` blocked),\\n- keep type-level fallback only when no account inventory exists yet,\\n- persist the account id on quota incidents and allocation records,\\n- make failover select another healthy account for the same worker type before falling back to another worker type when policy allows,\\n- keep `wait_for_reset` tied to the originally allocated account.\\n\\n## Settings And UI\\n\\nAgents settings remains the owner of worker ordering, but each worker row gains an account table:\\n\\n- account label,\\n- mode,\\n- identity/status,\\n- usage/quota,\\n- last used,\\n- enabled toggle,\\n- priority controls,\\n- status refresh,\\n- setup/login command.\\n\\nAdd account creation/editing as compact settings-dialog controls:\\n\\n- Use detected login,\\n- Isolated CLI login,\\n- API key,\\n- Existing credential profile,\\n- Credential command.\\n\\nComposer run settings should gain an `Account` selector when a concrete worker type is selected:\\n\\n- `Auto` uses the configured strategy,\\n- specific account pins the run to that account.\\n\\nPersist run-level choice with a new nullable `preferred_worker_account_id` column. The server treats the run value as an explicit allocation request.\\n\\nWire the run account choice through all run/message entry points:\\n\\n- frontend `useHomeMutations` create, send, direct, and commit flows,\\n- `src/runtime/http/routes/conversations.ts`,\\n- `src/runtime/http/routes/conversation-messages.ts`,\\n- `src/server/conversations/create.ts`,\\n- `src/server/conversations/send-message.ts`,\\n- CLI options and runner payloads if CLI-created runs should support account pinning.\\n\\nThe server must validate that a requested account exists, is enabled, and matches the selected worker type. Invalid explicit accounts fail visibly with `error.surfaced`; automatic allocation may fall back according to policy.\\n\\nAll new frontend text must be added to every `shared/locales/*.json` file and rendered through `t()`.\\n\\n## Migration\\n\\nAdd a startup migration from existing settings and rows:\\n\\n1. Existing `accounts` rows:\\n   - fill `cli_type` from `provider` when it matches a worker type, otherwise infer from `provider`/`auth_ref`,\\n   - map old `type` to `subscription | api | external`,\\n   - set `auth_mode = legacy_ref`,\\n   - keep `auth_ref` unchanged as a non-secret pointer,\\n   - set `enabled = true`, priority by insertion order.\\n\\n2. Existing default local logins:\\n   - on first account catalog refresh, create a `local_session` account per detected authenticated CLI if no equivalent account exists,\\n   - use `auth_ref = local-default`,\\n   - store only derived identity metadata such as email/account id hash/plan tier.\\n\\n3. Existing credential profile settings:\\n   - `OMNIHARNESS_CREDENTIAL_PROFILES_DIR` remains the profile root setting,\\n   - per-CLI command settings create `credential_command` accounts,\\n   - default profile folders named after a CLI create `credential_profile` accounts.\\n\\n4. Existing API key settings:\\n   - create API accounts referencing the existing encrypted setting keys where possible,\\n   - do not duplicate supervisor LLM keys into account secrets unless the user explicitly adds them as worker credentials.\\n\\n5. Existing worker settings:\\n   - keep `WORKER_ALLOWED_TYPES`, `WORKER_DEFAULT_TYPE`, and `WORKER_YOLO_MODE`,\\n   - migrate `CREDIT_STRATEGY` into a new per-CLI allocation policy setting or table-backed config,\\n   - map legacy `swap_account` to `priority` or `quota_balanced` according to the existing behavior at migration time,\\n   - keep `CREDIT_STRATEGY` as fallback compatibility until all readers move.\\n\\n6. Existing `config/accounts.yml` / `CreditManager`:\\n   - import rows into the account inventory idempotently,\\n   - treat `auth_ref` values as non-secret pointers unless they are known secret material,\\n   - preserve the file as a fallback compatibility source until all tests and runtime readers use the new inventory,\\n   - do not delete or rewrite the file during migration.\\n\\nMigration must be idempotent and emit named events for migration failures or skipped invalid rows.\\n\\n## Observability\\n\\nAdd named events:\\n\\n- `account.detected`\\n- `account.created`\\n- `account.updated`\\n- `account.status_checked`\\n- `account.credential_selected`\\n- `account.quota_exhausted`\\n- `account.switch_decision`\\n- `account.usage_recorded`\\n- `account.login_required`\\n\\nAdd `error.surfaced` codes for account resolver failures, missing login, invalid explicit account, quota switch failure, secret decryption failure, and migration failure.\\n\\nThe dev event log must be enough to answer: which account was chosen, why, what failed, and whether a switch/wait was deliberate.\\n\\nSnapshot and event invariants:\\n\\n- account payloads are always DTOs with no `authRef`, secret setting key, token, API key, or credential command output,\\n- named events may include `accountId`, account label, mode, status, reason, and strategy, but never raw secret refs,\\n- account allocation/switch/refusal decisions are named events, not inferred from snapshots,\\n- user-visible allocation failures emit `error.surfaced` with stable account-specific codes.\\n\\n## State Invariants\\n\\n- Server is authoritative for accounts, account status, allocation decisions, usage history, and run account choice.\\n- Client settings draft owns only unsaved form edits.\\n- Account list payloads carry a revision or updated timestamp; stale refreshes cannot overwrite newer edits.\\n- Account status refreshes are scoped by `accountId + requestId`.\\n- Allocation decisions are never inferred from snapshots; they are persisted and emitted as named events.\\n- Secrets never appear in account payloads, snapshots, SSE events, event log, test fixtures, or worker output.\\n- Cached availability may render as stale, but cannot erase known account records.\\n\\n## Testing\\n\\nAdd tests for:\\n\\n- schema migration from old `accounts` rows,\\n- migration from old settings keys,\\n- migration from `config/accounts.yml` and legacy `CREDIT_STRATEGY`,\\n- account resolver env ordering,\\n# Project-Scoped CLI Homes Must Bridge Credentials\\n\\n**Date:** 2026-05-26\\n**Context:** OmniHarness agent runtime recovery for Codex/Gemini workers\\n**Symptom:** Workers with persisted sessions failed to respawn after a crash. Gemini surfaced `Authentication required`; Codex exited before ACP startup completed.\\n**Root Cause:** Project-scoped CLI homes isolated session storage, but also isolated provider credentials. The scoped Gemini home had project metadata only, while auth lived in `~/.gemini`; the scoped Codex home had session SQLite only, while auth/config lived in `~/.codex`.\\n**Fix:** Keep project-scoped session storage, but bridge missing credential/config files into the scoped home with symlinks and copy fallback. This preserves durable per-project sessions without forcing each project to log in again.\\n**Verification:** `pnpm vitest run tests/server/agent-runtime/http.test.ts -t \\\"spawns Codex ACP workers|pins Gemini CLI session storage|bridges Codex credentials|bridges Gemini credentials|uses the requested session id\\\"` passes.\\n**Prevention:** When scoping provider homes, separate session/artifact isolation from auth/config availability. Recovery tests must assert both: sessions stay project-scoped and credentials remain reachable.\\n**Skill/Doc Updates:** No shared skill update needed; this rule is provider-runtime specific and is captured in the project learning notes.\\n# Claude Desktop Session Identity Must Resolve To The CLI Session\\n\\n**Date:** 2026-07-31\\n**Context:** OmniHarness external Claude session discovery and direct resume\\n**Symptom:** Sessions created in the macOS Claude Desktop app could not be found by their Desktop titles in the Resume CLI Session picker. After discovery was fixed, the provider session resumed but OmniHarness still called the new task \\\"New conversation\\\" and rendered \\\"No activity recorded for this session yet.\\\"\\n**Root Cause:** OmniHarness only read `~/.claude/projects/*.jsonl` for discovery, while Claude Desktop stores the user-facing session record separately under `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude-code-sessions/`. Its `local_…` session id is not the resumable Claude CLI id; `cliSessionId` points to the real JSONL session. The create path then treated a blank resume request like a blank new task: it generated the default title and connected ACP without importing the provider transcript into OmniHarness's unified worker stream.\\n**Fix:** Discovery overlays Desktop title, project path, and last-activity metadata onto the matching CLI transcript by `cliSessionId`, while continuing to send the CLI UUID—not the Desktop `local_…` id—to ACP resume. Creation now resolves that same record server-side, persists the provider title, and imports visible user/assistant messages plus tool calls and tool results into the unified worker stream before adding new lifecycle activity. Source-derived stable ids make retries and repairs idempotent. Import success or failure emits a typed named event, with a surfaced error when the local transcript cannot be loaded.\\n**Verification:** Regression tests failed first on the default title and missing stream entries. The discovery, API, named-event, and output-store suites then passed (81 tests), followed by the full TypeScript check and targeted ESLint run. Task `2053af87f210` was backfilled from Claude CLI session `471cb5bd-8ddd-4a82-a078-b43a5f77c467`; its title and imported entry counts were read back from the same database and worker stream used by the UI.\\n**Prevention:** Treat provider UI identity, display metadata, runtime resume identity, and local display history as separate responsibilities. Resolve them at the server boundary, hydrate the canonical local stream before reporting a resumed task as ready, preserve upstream ids for deduplication, and test both the runtime resume argument and the user-visible title/history.\\n**Skill/Doc Updates:** No general skill update was needed; this is a Claude Desktop storage contract, and this project note records the provider-specific Add one with `claude account add NAME`.\");\n        return Ok(());\n    }\n    for name in state.profiles.keys() {\n        let marker = if state.active.as_deref() == Some(name) {\n            \"*\"\n        } else {\n            \" \"\n        };\n        println!(\"{marker} {name}\");\n    }\n    Ok(())\n}\n\nfn current(paths: &AppPaths) -> Result<()> {\n    let state = state::load(paths)?;\n    match state.active {\n        Some(name) => {\n            println!(\"{name}\");\n            Ok(())\n        }\n        None => bail!(\"no active profile\"),\n    }\n}\n\nfn remove(paths: &AppPaths, name: &str, purge: bool, force: bool) -> Result<()> {\n    validate_profile_name(name)?;\n    let (profile, real_claude, is_active) = {\n        let _lock = StateLock::acquire(paths)?;\n        let state = state::load(paths)?;\n        let profile = state\n            .profiles\n            .get(name)\n            .cloned()\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"profile `{name}` does not exist\"))?;\n        let real_claude = state\n            .real_claude\n            .clone()\n            .context(\"real Claude executable is not configured\")?;\n        let is_active = state.active.as_deref() == Some(name);\n        if is_active && !force {\n            bail!(\n                \"`{name}` is active; switch profiles first, or pass --force to leave no active profile\"\n            );\n        }\n        (profile, real_claude, is_active)\n    };\n\n    println!(\"Logging out profile `{name}`...\");\n    let logout_status = process::managed_command(&real_claude, &profile.config_dir)\n        .args([\"auth\", \"logout\"])\n        .status()\n        .context(\"failed to start Claude logout\")?;\n    if !logout_status.success() {\n        bail!(\"Claude logout failed; profile `{name}` was not removed\");\n    }\n\n    {\n        let _lock = StateLock::acquire(paths)?;\n        let mut state = state::load(paths)?;\n        state.profiles.remove(name);\n        if is_active && state.active.as_deref() == Some(name) {\n            state.active = None;\n        }\n        state::save(paths, &state)?;\n    }\n\n    if purge {\n        let expected = paths.profile_dir(name);\n        if profile.config_dir != expected {\n            bail!(\n                \"refusing to purge unexpected directory {}; expected {}\",\n                profile.config_dir.display(),\n                expected.display()\n            );\n        }\n        let metadata = fs::symlink_metadata(&expected)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to inspect {}\", expected.display()))?;\n        if metadata.file_type().is_symlink() || !metadata.is_dir() {\n            bail!(\"refusing to purge a symlink or non-directory\");\n        }\n        fs::remove_dir_all(&expected)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to purge {}\", expected.display()))?;\n        println!(\"Removed `{name}` and permanently deleted its local data.\");\n    } else {\n        println!(\n            \"Removed `{name}`. Its non-credential data remains at {}.\",\n            profile.config_dir.display()\n        );\n    }\n    Ok(())\n}\n\nfn install(paths: &AppPaths, explicit_real: Option<&Path>) -> Result<()> {\n    let current_executable = env::current_exe().context(\"failed to locate this executable\")?;\n    let configured = {\n        let _lock = StateLock::acquire(paths)?;\n        state::load(paths)?.real_claude\n    };\n    let real_claude = match explicit_real {\n        Some(path) => {\n            if !path.is_absolute() {\n                bail!(\"--real must be an absolute path\");\n            }\n            process::validate_executable(path)?;\n            path.to_path_buf()\n        }\n        None => process::resolve_real_claude(configured.as_deref(), &current_executable, paths)?,\n    };\n\n    state::ensure_private_dir(&paths.data_dir)?;\n    state::ensure_private_dir(&paths.shim_dir)?;\n    let libexec_dir = paths\n        .installed_executable\n        .parent()\n        .context(\"invalid installation path\")?;\n    state::ensure_private_dir(libexec_dir)?;\n\n    let same_executable = fs::canonicalize(&current_executable).ok()\n        == fs::canonicalize(&paths.installed_executable).ok();\n    if !same_executable {\n        let temporary = paths\n            .installed_executable\n            .with_extension(format!(\"tmp.{}\", std::process::id()));\n        let mut destination = OpenOptions::new()\n            .create_new(true)\n            .write(true)\n            .mode(0o755)\n            .open(&temporary)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to create {}\", temporary.display()))?;\n        let mut source = fs::File::open(&current_executable)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to open {}\", current_executable.display()))?;\n        std::io::copy(&mut source, &mut destination).context(\"failed to install executable\")?;\n        destination\n            .sync_all()\n            .context(\"failed to sync executable\")?;\n        fs::set_permissions(&temporary, fs::Permissions::from_mode(0o755))?;\n        fs::rename(&temporary, &paths.installed_executable)\n            .context(\"failed to activate installed executable\")?;\n    }\n\n    if let Ok(metadata) = fs::symlink_metadata(&paths.shim) {\n        let points_to_us = metadata.file_type().is_symlink()\n            && fs::canonicalize(&paths.shim).ok()\n                == fs::canonicalize(&paths.installed_executable).ok();\n        if !points_to_us {\n            bail!(\n                \"refusing to replace existing non-managed path {}\",\n Some(real_claude.clone());\n        state::save(paths, &state)?;\n    }\n\n    println!(\"Installed claude-account.\");\n    println!(\"Real Claude: {}\", real_claude.display());\n    println!(\"Shim: Ok(())\n}\n\nfn validate_profile_name(name: &str) -> Result<()> {\n    let mut characters = name.chars();\n    let first = characters.next().context(\"profile name cannot be empty\")?;\n    if !first.is_ascii_alphanumeric()\n        || !characters.all(|character| {\n            character.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || character == '-' || character == '_'\n        })\n        || name.len() > 32\n    {\n        bail!(\n            \"invalid profile name `{name}`; use 1-32 letters, numbers, hyphens, or underscores, \\\n             starting with a letter or number\"\n        );\n    }\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn profile_name_validation_blocks_path_traversal() {\n        for invalid in [\"\", \"../work\", \".work\", \"work space\", \"work/personal\"] {\n            assert!(validate_profile_name(invalid).is_err(), \"{invalid}\");\n        }\n        for valid in [\"work\", \"personal-2\", \"team_account\"] {\n            assert!(validate_profile_name(valid).is_ok(), \"{valid}\");\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn add_uses_an_isolated_config_directory() {\n        let temp = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();\n        let paths = AppPaths::from_roots(temp.path().join(\"config\"), temp.path().join(\"data\"));\n        let fake_claude = temp.path().join(\"claude-real\");\n        let log = '%s|%s\\\\n' \\\"$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR\\\" \\\"$*\\\" >> '{}'\\n\\\n             if [ \\\"$1 $2 $3\\\" = \\\"auth status --json\\\" ]; then\\n\\\n               printf '{{\\\"loggedIn\\\":true}}\\\\n'\\n\\\n             fi\\n\\\n             exit 0\",\n            log.display()\n        )\n        .unwrap();\n        drop(script);\n        fs::set_permissions(&fake_claude, fs::Permissions::from_mode(0o755)).unwrap();\n\n        {\n            let _lock = StateLock::acquire(&paths).unwrap();\n            let mut initial = state::load(&paths).unwrap();\n            initial.real_claude = Some(fake_claude);\n            state::save(&paths, &initial).unwrap();\n        }\n\n        add(&paths, \"work\", None, false, assert_eq!(claude_config[\"hasCompletedOnboarding\"], true);\n        assert_eq!(state::load(&paths).unwrap().active.as_deref(), Some(\"work\"));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn     "text": "use std::env;\nuse std::ffi::OsString;\nuse std::fs;\nuse std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt;\nuse std::os::unix::process::CommandExt;\nuse std::path::{Path, PathBuf};\nuse std::process::Command;\n\nuse anyhow::{bail, Context, Result};\n\nuse crate::paths::AppPaths;\nuse crate::state;\n\nconst AUTH_ENVIRONMENT: [&str; 3] = [\n    \"ANTHROPIC_API_KEY\",\n    \"ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN\",\n    \"CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN\",\n];\n\npub fn exec_active_profile(paths: &AppPaths, arguments: &[OsString]) -> Result<()> {\n    let state = state::load(paths)?;\n    let active = state\n        .active\n        .as_deref()\n        .context(\"no active profile; run `claude account add NAME` or `claude account use NAME`\")?;\n    let profile = state\n        .profiles\n        .get(active)\n        .with_context(|| format!(\"active profile `{active}` does not exist\"))?;\n    let real_claude = state\n        .real_claude\n        .as_deref()\n        .context(\"real Claude executable is not configured; run `claude-account install`\")?;\n    validate_executable(real_claude)?;\n\n    let mut command = managed_command(real_claude, &profile.config_dir);\n    command.args(arguments);\n    let error = command.exec();\n    Err(error).with_context(|| format!(\"failed to execute {}\", real_claude.display()))\n}\n\npub fn managed_command(real_claude: &Path, config_dir: &Path) -> Command {\n    let mut command = Command::new(real_claude);\n    command.env(\"CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR\", config_dir);\n\n    if env::var_os(\"CLAUDE_ACCOUNT_PRESERVE_AUTH_ENV\").as_deref() != Some(\"1\".as_ref()) {\n        for variable in AUTH_ENVIRONMENT {\n            command.env_remove(variable);\n        }\n    }\n    command\n}\n\npub fn resolve_real_claude(\n    configured: Option<&Path>,\n    current_executable: &Path,\n    paths: &AppPaths,\n) -> Result<PathBuf> {\n    if let Some(explicit) = env::var_os(\"CLAUDE_ACCOUNT_REAL_CLAUDE\") {\n        let explicit = PathBuf::from(explicit);\n        validate_distinct_executable(&explicit, current_executable)?;\n        return Ok(explicit);\n    }\n\n    if let Some(configured) = configured {\n        if validate_distinct_executable(configured, current_executable).is_ok() {\n            return Ok(configured.to_path_buf());\n        }\n    }\n\n    let path = env::var_os(\"PATH\").context(\"PATH is not set\")?;\n    for directory in env::split_paths(&path) {\n        let candidate = if directory.as_os_str().is_empty() {\n            env::current_dir()?.join(\"claude\")\n        } else {\n            directory.join(\"claude\")\n        };\n        if candidate == paths.shim {\n            continue;\n        }\n        if validate_distinct_executable(&candidate, current_executable).is_ok() {\n            return Ok(candidate);\n        }\n    }\n\n    bail!(\n        \"could not find the real `claude` executable; pass it with \\\n         `claude-account install --real /path/to/claude`\"\n    )\n}\n\npub fn validate_executable(path: &Path) -> Result<()> {\n    let metadata = fs::metadata(path)\n        .with_context(|| format!(\"Claude executable does not exist: {}\", path.display()))?;\n    if !metadata.is_file() || metadata.permissions().mode() & 0o111 == 0 {\n        bail!(\"path is not executable: {}\", path.display());\n    }\n    Ok(())\n}\n\nfn validate_distinct_executable(candidate: &Path, current_executable: &Path) -> Result<()> {\n    validate_executable(candidate)?;\n    let candidate_canonical = fs::canonicalize(candidate)\n        .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to resolve {}\", candidate.display()))?;\n    let current_canonical = fs::canonicalize(current_executable)\n        .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to resolve {}\", current_executable.display()))?;\n    if candidate_canonical == current_canonical {\n        bail!(\"candidate points back to the claude-account wrapper\");\n    }\n    Ok(())\n}\n"

PermissionsExt};\nuse std::path::{Path, PathBuf};\nuse std::time::{SystemTime, UNIX_EPOCH};\n\nuse anyhow::{Context, Result};\nuse serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};\n\nuse crate::paths::AppPaths;\n\nconst LOCK_EX: i32 = 2;\n\nunsafe extern \"C\" {\n    fn flock(fd: i32, operation: i32) -> i32;\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Default, Serialize, Deserialize)]\npub struct State {\n    #[serde(default = \"state_version\")]\n    pub version: u32,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub active: Option<String>,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub real_claude: Option<PathBuf>,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub profiles: BTreeMap<String, Profile>,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]\npub struct Profile {\n    pub config_dir: PathBuf,\n    pub created_at: u64,\n}\n\nimpl Profile {\n    pub fn new(config_dir: PathBuf) -> Self {\n        let created_at = SystemTime::now()\n            .duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)\n            .unwrap_or_default()\n            .as_secs();\n        Self {\n            config_dir,\n            created_at,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nfn state_version() -> u32 {\n    1\n}\n\npub struct StateLock {\n    _file: File,\n}\n\nimpl StateLock {\n    pub fn acquire(paths: &AppPaths) -> Result<Self> {\n        ensure_private_dir(&paths.config_dir)?;\n        let file = OpenOptions::new()\n            .create(true)\n            .read(true)\n            .write(true)\n            .truncate(false)\n            .mode(0o600)\n            .open(&paths.lock_file)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to open {}\", paths.lock_file.display()))?;\n\n        loop {\n            let result = unsafe { flock(file.as_raw_fd(), LOCK_EX) };\n            if result == 0 {\n                break;\n            }\n            let error = io::Error::last_os_error();\n            if error.kind() != io::ErrorKind::Interrupted {\n                return Err(error).context(\"failed to lock profile state\");\n            }\n        }\n\n        Ok(Self { _file: file })\n    }\n}\n\npub fn load(paths: &AppPaths) -> Result<State> {\n    match File::open(&paths.state_file) {\n        Ok(file) => {\n            let state: State = serde_json::from_reader(file)\n                .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to parse {}\", paths.state_file.display()))?;\n            if state.version != 1 {\n                anyhow::bail!(\"unsupported state version {}\", state.version);\n            }\n            Ok(state)\n        }\n        Err(error) if error.kind() == io::ErrorKind::NotFound => Ok(State {\n            version: state_version(),\n            ..State::default()\n        }),\n        Err(error) => {\n            Err(error).with_context(|| format!(\"failed to read {}\", paths.state_file.display()))\n        }\n    }\n}\n\npub fn save(paths: &AppPaths, state: &State) -> Result<()> {\n    ensure_private_dir(&paths.config_dir)?;\n    let temporary = temporary_state_path(&paths.state_file);\n    let result = (|| -> Result<()> {\n        let mut file = OpenOptions::new()\n            .create_new(true)\n            .write(true)\n            .mode(0o600)\n            .open(&temporary)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to create {}\", temporary.display()))?;\n        serde_json::to_writer_pretty(&mut file, state).context(\"failed to serialize state\")?;\n        file.write_all(b\"\\n\")\n            .context(\"failed to finish state file\")?;\n        file.sync_all().context(\"failed to sync state file\")?;\n        fs::rename(&temporary, &paths.state_file).with_context(|| {\n            format!(\n                \"failed to replace {} with {}\",\n                paths.state_file.display(),\n                temporary.display()\n            )\n        })?;\n        fs::set_permissions(&paths.state_file, fs::Permissions::from_mode(0o600))\n            .context(\"failed to protect state file\")?;\n        Ok(())\n    })();\n\n    if result.is_err() {\n        let _ = fs::remove_file(&temporary);\n    }\n    result\n}\n\npub fn ensure_private_dir(path: &Path) -> Result<()> {\n    fs::create_dir_all(path)\n        .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to create directory {}\", path.display()))?;\n    fs::set_permissions(path, fs::Permissions::from_mode(0o700))\n        .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to protect directory {}\", path.display()))?;\n    Ok(())\n}\n\nfn temporary_state_path(state_file: &Path) -> PathBuf {\n    let filename = state_file\n        .file_name()\n        .and_then(|name| name.to_str())\n        .unwrap_or(\"state.json\");\n    let nonce = SystemTime::now()\n        .duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)\n        .unwrap_or_default()\n        .as_nanos();\n    state_file.with_file_name(format!(\"{filename}.tmp.{}.{}\", std::process::id(), nonce))\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn state_round_trip_preserves_profiles() {\n        let temp = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();\n        let paths = AppPaths::from_roots(temp.path().join(\"config\"), temp.path().join(\"data\"));\n        let mut state = State {\n            version: 1,\n            ..State::default()\n        };\n        state.active = Some(\"work\".to_owned());\n        state\n            .profiles\n            .insert(\"work\".to_owned(), Profile::new(paths.profile_dir(\"work\")));\n\n        let _lock = StateLock::acquire(&paths).unwrap();\n        save(&paths, &state).unwrap();\n        let loaded = load(&paths).unwrap();\n\n        assert_eq!(loaded.active.as_deref(), Some(\"work\"));\n        assert!(loaded.profiles.contains_key(\"work\"));\n    }\n}\n"

    "text": "use std::env;\nuse std::path::{Path, PathBuf};\n\nuse anyhow::{bail, Context, Result};\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct AppPaths {\n    pub config_dir: PathBuf,\n    pub data_dir: PathBuf,\n    pub state_file: PathBuf,\n    pub lock_file: PathBuf,\n    pub profiles_dir: PathBuf,\n    pub shim_dir: PathBuf,\n    pub shim: PathBuf,\n    pub installed_executable: PathBuf,\n}\n\nimpl AppPaths {\n    pub fn discover() -> Result<Self> {\n        if let Some(root) = env::var_os(\"CLAUDE_ACCOUNT_HOME\") {\n            let root = absolute_path(root, \"CLAUDE_ACCOUNT_HOME\")?;\n            return Ok(Self::from_roots(root.clone(), root));\n        }\n\n        let home = env::var_os(\"HOME\")\n            .map(PathBuf::from)\n            .filter(|path| path.is_absolute())\n            .context(\"HOME is not set to an absolute path\")?;\n\n        let config_root = env::var_os(\"XDG_CONFIG_HOME\")\n            .map(PathBuf::from)\n            .filter(|path| path.is_absolute())\n            .unwrap_or_else(|| home.join(\".config\"))\n            .join(\"claude-account\");\n\n        let data_root = env::var_os(\"XDG_DATA_HOME\")\n            .map(PathBuf::from)\n            .filter(|path| path.is_absolute())\n            .unwrap_or_else(|| home.join(\".local/share\"))\n            .join(\"claude-account\");\n\n        Ok(Self::from_roots(config_root, data_root))\n    }\n\n    pub fn from_roots(config_dir: PathBuf, data_dir: PathBuf) -> Self {\n        let shim_dir = data_dir.join(\"bin\");\n        Self {\n            state_file: config_dir.join(\"state.json\"),\n            lock_file: config_dir.join(\"state.lock\"),\n            profiles_dir: data_dir.join(\"profiles\"),\n            shim: shim_dir.join(\"claude\"),\n            installed_executable: data_dir.join(\"libexec/claude-account\"),\n            config_dir,\n            data_dir,\n            shim_dir,\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn profile_dir(&self, name: &str) -> PathBuf {\n        self.profiles_dir.join(name)\n    }\n}\n\nfn absolute_path(value: impl AsRef<Path>, variable: &str) -> Result<PathBuf> {\n    let path = PathBuf::from(value.as_ref());\n    if !path.is_absolute() {\n        bail!(\"{variable} must contain an absolute path\");\n    }\n    Ok(path)\n}\n"

    "text": "# Changelog\n\nAll notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.\n\nThe format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/),\nand this project follows [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).\n\n## [Unreleased]\n\n## [0.1.1] - 2026-07-30\n\n### Fixed\n\n- Complete Claude Code onboarding after a verified `account add` login so the\n  first normal `claude` launch does not ask the user to authenticate again.\n- Require `auth status --json` to explicitly report `loggedIn: true` before a\n  profile is registered.\n\n## [0.1.0] - 2026-07-30\n\n### Added\n\n- Linux-only Claude Code profile isolation through `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`.\n- `add`, `use`, `list`, `current`, and `remove` account commands.\n- Transparent forwarding of normal Claude Code commands and arguments.\n- Official Claude Code login, status verification, and logout integration.\n- Atomic state writes, process locking, strict filesystem permissions, and\n  profile-name validation.\n- Safe profile removal with separate unregister and permanent purge modes.\n- Non-invasive shim installation that preserves the official Claude launcher.\n- Unit and end-to-end lifecycle tests.\n\n[Unreleased]: https://github.com/hamzarehmandeveloper/claude-account/compare/v0.1.1...HEAD\n[0.1.1]: https://github.com/hamzarehmandeveloper/claude-account/compare/v0.1.0...v0.1.1\n[0.1.0]: https://github.com/hamzarehmandeveloper/claude-account/releases/tag/v0.1.0\n"
  },
  {
    "type": "input_text",
    "text": "===== SECURITY.md ====="
  },
  {
    "type": "input_text",
    "text": "# Security policy\n\n## Supported versions\n\nSecurity fixes are provided for the latest released version.\n\n## Reporting a vulnerability\n\nPlease use GitHub's private **Report a vulnerability** feature on the\nrepository's Security tab. Do not open a public issue for a suspected\ncredential exposure, path traversal, arbitrary command execution, or unsafe\ndeletion vulnerability.\n\nInclude:\n\n- The affected version and Linux distribution\n- Reproduction steps using placeholder credentials\n- The expected and observed behavior\n- Any proposed fix, if available\n\nNever include real Claude credentials, access tokens, refresh tokens, API keys,\nor the contents of `.credentials.json`.\n\n## Security model\n\nclaude-account does not parse or copy Claude credentials. It creates an\nisolated `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` and delegates authentication to the official\nClaude Code executable. Local profile directories are owner-only (`0700`) and\nthe registry is owner-readable and owner-writable (`0600`).\n\nThe program runs with the invoking user's permissions. Anyone who can modify\nthat user's configuration or executable search path is already within the same\nlocal trust boundary.\n"
  },
  {
    "type": "input_text",

## Codex progress · 2026-07-31T14:00:31.399Z

The comparison points to a narrow but valuable gap: OmniHarness already has the account database, selection, quota, recovery, and worker-isolation machinery. What it lacks is the polished lifecycle for creating and validating a second Claude subscription login inside an isolated directory—the small project handles exactly that part.

<!-- codex-event:{"kind":"final","timestamp":"2026-07-31T14:01:16.324Z","phase":"final_answer"} -->
## Codex final · 2026-07-31T14:01:16.324Z

Yes—useful as a reference implementation for the Claude login lifecycle, but not as OmniHarness’s overall multi-account architecture.

OmniHarness already has the more advanced parts:

- Account inventory, automatic selection, quota handling, and per-run account pinning.
- Account-specific `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` support in [account-resolver.ts](/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/server/accounts/account-resolver.ts:30).
- Correct isolation from project storage and the global keychain during worker launch in [manager.ts](/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/server/agent-runtime/manager.ts:1598).
- The same isolated-home approach is already specified in [the multi-account design](/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-29-multi-account-cli-credentials.md:111).

What `claude-account` does better is the missing setup experience:

- Runs Claude’s official `auth login` inside the isolated directory.
- Verifies success with `claude auth status --json` before registering the account.
- Lets Claude own credential storage and token refresh; it never reads or copies tokens.
- Removes ambient `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, and `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` so they cannot silently override the selected account.
- Separates logout/unregister from permanent profile deletion.
- Handles onboarding so the first real launch does not ask users to log in again. See its [account lifecycle](https://github.com/hamzarehmandeveloper/claude-account/blob/main/src/account.rs) and [process environment handling](https://github.com/hamzarehmandeveloper/claude-account/blob/main/src/process.rs).

That exposes two concrete OmniHarness gaps:

1. The UI currently only adds the existing local login; it cannot create and authenticate a second isolated Claude account. See [AgentsSettingsPanel.tsx](/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/components/settings/AgentsSettingsPanel.tsx:150).

2. “Refresh account status” currently records the existing/requested status without actually running `claude auth status`. See [accounts.ts](/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/runtime/http/routes/accounts.ts:390).

There is also a likely credential-selection risk: OmniHarness’s `isolated_cli_home` path changes `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` but does not clear ambient Anthropic authentication variables ([account-resolver.ts](/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/server/accounts/account-resolver.ts:121)). Those variables could override the selected subscription account. The external project’s environment cleaning is worth adopting, probably including `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` as well.

I would borrow the lifecycle, not the package:

- Add “Connect another Claude account.”
- Create an isolated directory.
- Run official Claude login with conflicting authentication variables removed.
- Verify the returned login and capture only safe identity metadata.
- Enable the account only after verification.
- Make status refresh perform a real check.
- Keep “remove from OmniHarness,” “log out,” and “delete profile data” as separate actions.

I would not install or wrap OmniHarness with this project. It is Linux-only, version `0.1.1`, and its entire public history began on July 30, 2026 ([commit history](https://github.com/hamzarehmandeveloper/claude-account/commits/main)). Its shim, JSON registry, and filesystem locking duplicate infrastructure OmniHarness already handles more appropriately through its server and database.

Bottom line: it strongly validates our isolated-directory design and supplies an excellent model for the missing login/status/logout adapter. It should inspire a small native OmniHarness service, not become a dependency.

Serve these paths from a bounded read model, memory cache, append-only event log, or stale-but-marked snapshot; queue reconciliation writes outside the request. Browser automation is for UI behavior; control-plane tests assert server decisions directly.\n\nWrite scenario assertions as event transcripts:\n\n```ts\nexpect(events).toHaveEmitted(\"worker.spawned\", { runId });\nexpect(events).toHaveEmitted(\"worker.status\", { next: \"running\" });\nchaos.killServer();\nchaos.restartServer();\nexpect(events).toHaveEmitted(\"worker.reattached\", { runId });\nexpect(events).not.toHaveEmitted(\"worker.recreated\", { runId });\n```\n\nChaos belongs outside production code paths: drop connections in the client, fail fetches in the harness, restart the server process, and use seeds for reproducibility.\n\n## Refuse These Shapes\n\n- silent early returns in server methods;\n- swallowed `catch` blocks;\n- client-side derivation of server decisions;\n- response-code-only user failures;\n- event streams without ids or resume;\n- tests that infer control-plane behavior from rendered state;\n- delete handlers that do not enumerate dependent rows or emit typed failure events;\n- recovery loops without terminal events such as `gave_up` or `abandoned`;\n- request handlers that wait on inline reconciliation writes, SQLite contention, or bridge `/doctor` checks before returning bootstrap data;\n- test-only behavior branches in production code.\n\n## Design Checklist\n\nBefore implementing a backend or agent workflow, answer:\n\n1. Does it change what the user should do?\n\nIf all answers are no, delete it.\n\n## Persistence And Scope\n\nEvery meaningful setting still needs explicit behavior:\n\n- whether it persists,\n- where it is stored,\n- who owns it,\n- when it is loaded and saved,\n- whether it is local, workspace-level, account-level, or synced,\n- how reset, migration, and verification work.\n\nThis persistence design belongs in the plan or spec, not as explanatory prose inside the dialog unless the user needs it to make a safe choice.\n\n## Common Mistakes\n\n| Mistake | Better |\n|---|---|\n| Tab says \"Appearance\", panel title says \"Appearance\", subtitle says \"Customize how the app looks.\" | Use the tab label only. A registry starts every profile connection, not only the\nvisible one. Switching the visible workspace changes active managers/query\ncaches and terminal ownership without closing inactive main streams.\n\nEvery bootstrap, snapshot, frame, retry, timer, and mutation checks profile and\nlearned runner identity before applying state. Stored cursors include the\nrunner's stream epoch. `runner.stopping`, `auth.session_revoked`, and\n`stream.resync_required` are typed terminal/control outcomes, not generic\nnetwork failures.\n\nElectron, VS Code, and Capacitor host bridges have bounded stream delivery and\nmust cancel upstream work on overflow. Mobile suspension persists cursors,\ncloses streams, and reconnects on resume; it must not claim background\ndelivery. Platform lifecycle contract tests live under `tests/electron`,\n`tests/vscode`, `tests/mobile`, and `tests/runtime-api`; real two-runner and\neight-runner journeys live under `tests/e2e`.\n\n## Interactive protocol invariant\n\nAn advertised interactive agent capability is operational only when the complete user journey is implemented: receive the request, append it to the unified worker stream, render an actionable control in the main conversation, submit the exact protocol response, and append a terminal outcome before resolving the agent request. Side-panel-only controls do not satisfy this invariant. Every form shape and permission option emitted by a supported adapter must be covered by a finite wire-to-UI regression matrix.\n\nRelated: `docs/architecture/timing-determinism-audit.md` records the May 20,\n2026 audit of race-prone frontend and control-plane patterns: cached snapshots\npretending to be authoritative, stale async callbacks, timer-owned actions,\ntimestamp-only ordering, and silent wake/lease contention.\n\n## Why this document exists\n\nOver a single afternoon we hit three production-class bugs that the existing test\nsuite did not catch and could not have caught:\n\n1. **Session fails to reconnect after a server restart and gives up after the\n   first attempt.** No user-visible message, no telemetry event, no recovery\n   incident — just a silently dead session.\n2. **`DELETE /conversations/:id` fails with a foreign-key constraint** because\n   related rows in dependent tables were not cleared first. The error surfaces\n   as an opaque 500.\n3. **Running plan-improvement agents fails because leftover state blocks the\n   new run.** The block is silent; the user sees nothing happen and assumes the\n   button is broken.\n\nThese are not unrelated bugs. They share a single root cause:\n\n> **The server makes state transitions that nobody observes.** Neither the user,\n> nor the UI, nor any test client can tell what the server decided. So bugs in\n> the *decision* (gave up too early, took the wrong branch, refused silently)\n> are invisible.\n\nThis document records what we learned and the rules we now follow so that this\nclass of bug stops shipping.\n\nRelated incident note: `docs/architecture/supervisor-worker-switching-incident.md`\nrecords the worker-switching failure from session `690d2fa9f2a7`, where\n`awaiting_user` was treated as runnable, Gemini workers were live but persisted\nas `starting`, and duplicate continuation workers were spawned.\n\nRelated direct-control note:\n`docs/architecture/direct-control-session-regressions.md` records the\n`ffb912d4d5d7`, `937e642f3535`, and `734cc38f4d7f` regressions around\nlifecycle noise, stale queued send-now state, missing unified-stream worker\noutput, and permanent \"Thinking...\" indicators.\n\nRelated state-staleness note:\n`docs/architecture/state-staleness-and-session-lifecycle-lessons.md` records\nthe `0785684884fa`, `14260d2a2df0`, `ecea142f7344`, and `18fc406457f3`\nregressions around stale SSE/cache payloads, queued-message races, direct-run\nstatus classification, unread markers, and worker-stream loading.\n\n---\n\n## What we found in the audit\n\nA targeted audit of `src/app/api/events/route.ts` plus the planning, recovery,\nand bridge-client subsystems revealed the structural gaps.\n\n### 1. The SSE stream is a snapshot stream, not an event stream\n\n`/api/events` emits exactly one named event: `update`, whose payload is the\n*entire* current state of the world for the selected run (messages, plans,\nruns, workers, planItems, clarifications, executionEvents, supervisor\ninterventions, queued messages, recovery incidents, review runs/rounds/findings).\n\nThere are no other named events. An observer cannot ask \"did a worker spawn?\"\nor \"was a recovery attempted?\" — only \"is the state now different?\" To answer\nthe first kind of question the client must **diff snapshots**, which is:\n\n- **Ambiguous** — many transitions produce identical visible state (a worker\n  that was reattached and a worker that was recreated both end up as\n  `status=\"running\"`).\n- **Lossy** — fast transitions can be coalesced inside a single snapshot\n  interval and disappear entirely. (e.g. `starting → running → completed`\n  inside one 15s window.)\n- **Forced to re-derive server decisions** — the client has to reconstruct\n  *why* state changed, which requires duplicating server logic.\n\n### 2. There is no event ID and no resume\n\nThe SSE frames have no `id:` field. There is no `Last-Event-ID` handling on the\nserver. A client that disconnects and reconnects gets a fresh snapshot and has\n*no way to know* whether events fired during the gap. For chaos testing (where\nwe deliberately drop the connection) this is fatal — we cannot assert\n\"between t0 and t1 the server emitted [X, Y, Z]\" because the wire format does\nnot carry that information.\n\nThere is a `?snapshot=1` bootstrap endpoint, which is good. There is no\n\"give me the events I missed since id N\" endpoint, which is the gap.\n\n### 3. Several decisions are invisible to the wire\n\nConcrete state transitions that **the server makes** but **never tells anyone\nabout**:\n\n| Transition | Where it happens | Wire visibility |\n|---|---|---|\n| Worker spawned | `bridge-client/index.ts spawnAgent` | None — inferred from a row appearing |\n| Worker reattached vs recreated after restart | `restart-control.ts` / recovery path | **None** — both look like `status=\"running\"` |\n| Recovery gave up after N attempts | `recoveryIncidents.autoAttemptCount` increments | Partial — count is visible but there is no terminal \"abandoned\" state |\n| Plan readiness reached | `derivePlanningStatus()` — runs **client-side** | **None** — it is a client-side derivation, not a server event |\n| Plan-improvement blocked by leftover state | `planning/review.ts` early-return | **None** — silent refusal |\n| Conversation delete FK violation | `/api/conversations/[id]` DELETE | None as a typed event — only a 500 response |\n| Message ack / persisted / streaming chunk | `conversations/send-message.ts` | Partial — only the resulting queued-message status |\n\nEvery row in this table is a bug class waiting to ship. If the server can\nsilently decide \"I gave up\", \"I refused\", \"I took branch B not A\", and the\ntest harness has no way to assert which branch it took, the test harness is\nstructurally incapable of catching the bug.\n\n### 4. The user-facing surface mirrors the test-facing surface\n\nThe reason \"leftover state blocked the run\" did not show a user message is the\n**same reason** no test could detect it: there was no event for it. Make the\nstate transitions observable, and both the UI fix and the test coverage\nfollow. Conversely, if a transition is observable only by re-deriving from a\nsnapshot diff, both the UI and tests will be brittle in the same ways.\n\nThis is the central insight: **observability for users and observability for\ntests are the same problem**.\n\n### 5. Playwright e2e is the wrong layer for resilience\n\nThe existing `tests/e2e/*.spec.ts` files boot Chromium. They are slow (tens of\nseconds per scenario), flaky against real subprocess restarts, and they\nexercise UI rendering rather than control-plane decisions. The bugs we are\nhitting are not UI bugs — they are control-plane bugs. We should be hitting\nHTTP/SSE directly, in Node, with no browser. The UI is one consumer of the\ncontrol plane; the chaos harness is another.\n\n---\n\n## The rules we now follow\n\nThese are not suggestions. They are the discipline that makes this class of\nbug stop happening.\n\n### Rule 1: every server-side state transition emits a named event\n\nIf the server makes a decision — spawn, reattach, recreate, give up, refuse,\ndelete, fail — that decision is published on the event stream with a\n**named event type**, not just a state delta. Examples:\n\n- `worker.spawned`, `worker.status` (with `prev` and `next`), `worker.terminal`\n- `worker.reattached`, `worker.recreated`\n- `plan.ready`, `plan.review.started`, `plan.review.finished`,\n  `plan.review.blocked` (with a `reason`)\n- `recovery.opened`, `recovery.attempt`, `recovery.gave_up`, `recovery.resolved`\n- `conversation.deleted`, `conversation.delete_failed` (with FK details)\n- `error.surfaced` — the catch-all for anything the user should know about\n\n**Rule of thumb:** if a server method has an early-return, a try/catch that\nswallows, or a branch that depends on a state check, it emits an event.\n\"Silent\" is a code smell.\n\n### Rule 2: errors that affect the user are events, not just response codes\n\nA 500 with a body is not enough. A 200 that quietly did nothing is worse. Every\nuser-relevant failure publishes `error.surfaced` with a stable code, a\nhuman-readable message, and the relevant run/worker/conversation ids. The UI's\njob is to render `error.surfaced` events into toasts/banners. The test\nharness's job is to assert that the expected `error.surfaced` event fired.\n\nA failure that does not produce an `error.surfaced` event is a bug — even if\nthe underlying behaviour is technically correct — because it is invisible to\nthe user and to the tests.\n\nThe event carries the stable id of the subject that failed. Conversation and\nworker failures use `runId`, `conversationId`, or `workerId`; account-only\nsettings failures use `accountId` rather than pretending an account is a\nconversation.\n\n### Rule 3: the event stream is SSE-spec compliant\n\n- Every frame has an `id:` field. IDs are monotonic.\n- The server keeps a bounded **ring buffer** (≥ 500 entries) of recent events.\n- The server honours `Last-Event-ID` on reconnect: it replays everything after\n  that id from the buffer, then resumes live streaming.\n- If the requested id has fallen out of the buffer, the server emits a\n  `stream.resync_required` event so the client knows to re-bootstrap from\n  `?snapshot=1` rather than silently miss events.\n\nThis is the SSE spec. We were not following it. We are now.\n\n### Rule 4: named events alongside, not instead of, snapshots\n\nThe existing `update` snapshot event stays. The UI keeps consuming it. The new\nnamed events are *additional* frames on the same stream. Clients that don't\ncare about a given event type ignore it. There is no `?test=1` flag, no\nseparate test endpoint, no parallel surface that can drift.\n\nIf a transition is worth emitting for tests, it is worth emitting in\nproduction. Anything else creates a second observability surface that will\ndiverge from reality.\n\n### Rule 5: chaos testing belongs in the client, not the server\n\nWe do **not** add fault-injection code paths to the server. We do not add a\n\"random failure\" mode. The server stays clean. Chaos lives in the test\nclient as middleware:\n\n- An SSE wrapper that can drop the connection on command.\n- A `fetch` wrapper that can fail a configurable percentage of requests.\n- A harness that can SIGKILL the spawned server process and restart it.\n\nFaults are seeded for reproducibility. Every failure has a seed; replaying\nthe seed reproduces the failure.\n\n### Rule 6: tests assert on event sequences, not on rendered state\n\nA scenario test reads like a transcript:\n\n```\nexpect(events).toHaveEmitted(\"worker.spawned\", { runId });\nexpect(events).toHaveEmitted(\"worker.status\", { next: \"running\" });\nchaos.killServer();\nchaos.restartServer();\nexpect(events).toHaveEmitted(\"worker.reattached\", { runId });\n// not \"worker.recreated\", not absence — explicitly reattached\n```\n\n### Rule 7: cleanup waits for server-owned background work\n\nLifecycle scenarios may call routes that intentionally return before a direct\nworker turn finishes. That is fine for product latency, but it is not fine for\ntest cleanup to delete `OMNIHARNESS_ROOT` while those server-owned tasks are\nstill writing worker JSONL, recovery rows, or named Here's what I'd propose:\n\n## Current Behavior (which I think is mostly correct!)\n\n  * User configuration files (skills, agents, commands) remain in `~/.config/claude-code/` - this is the correct location per XDG spec and allows version control\n  * State/runtime files (currently in `~/.claude/`) can be relocated via `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` to follow XDG conventions (e.g., `~/.local/state/claude-code/`)\n  * Project-specific files (`.claude/settings.local.json`) remain in project directories - this is correct for project-scoped configuration\n  * Exception: `~/.claude.json` is hardcoded to the home directory and is not affected by `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`\n\nThis separation is actually quite good and follows best practices, though the `.claude.json` location is problematic.\n\n## Proposed Improvements\n\n### 1. Rename the environment variable\n\n`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` → `CLAUDE_STATE_DIR`\n\nThis better reflects what it actually controls: runtime state, not user configuration. The XDG Base Directory spec distinguishes between:\n\n  * `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME` (default: `~/.config`) - user configuration files that should be preserved\n  * `$XDG_STATE_HOME` (default: `~/.local/state`) - state data that can be regenerated but contains valuable user-specific state\n\nWhat `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` currently relocates (history, projects, shell-snapshots, statsig, etc.) clearly fits the \"state\" category per XDG.\n\n### 2. Move `settings.json` to the config directory\n\nCurrently `settings.json` lives in the state directory (`~/.claude/settings.json`), but it should live in `~/.config/claude-code/settings.json` alongside other user configuration files (skills, agents, commands). The `settings.json` file contains user preferences and configuration that should be:\n\n  * Preserved across reinstalls\n  * Version controlled\n  * Synced across machines\n\nThis is configuration, not state.\n\n### 3. Make `~/.claude.json` respect `CLAUDE_STATE_DIR`\n\nCurrently, `~/.claude.json` is hardcoded to the home directory and doesn't respect `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`. This file contains:\n\n  * API keys and authentication\n  * MCP server configurations\n  * Project history\n  * Approved/rejected API key responses\n\nThis is clearly state data (especially the auth tokens and project history), so it should be relocatable to `$CLAUDE_STATE_DIR/claude.json` (without the leading dot, since it's no longer in `~/`).\n\nProposed structure:\n    \n    `~/.config/claude-code/\n    ├── settings.json         # User settings (moved from state dir)\n    ├── agents/\n    ├── commands/\n    └── skills/\n    \n    ~/.local/state/claude-code/\n    ├── claude.json           # Main state file (moved from ~/.claude.json, renamed)\n    ├── claude.json.backup\n    ├── history.jsonl\n    ├── projects/\n    ├── shell-snapshots/\n    └── ...\n    `\n\n### 4. Document the intended behavior\n\nPlease officially document:\n\n  * The purpose of `CLAUDE_STATE_DIR` (or keep `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` if you prefer that name)\n  * Which files/directories it affects (including `~/.claude.json` → `$CLAUDE_STATE_DIR/claude.json`)\n  * The distinction between state (relocated) and config (stays in `~/.config/claude-code/`)\n  * That project-local `.claude/` directories are intentionally not affected\n  * Where `settings.json` should live (config directory)\n\n### 5. Check your proxy client settings for the correct port number.\n\nThen clean up and re-authenticate:\n    \n    rm -rf ~/.claude\n    claude auth login\n\nVerify with `/status` inside Claude Code — you should see:\n\n  * Login method: Claude Max Account (not \"Claude API Account\")\n  * Proxy: http://127.0.0.1:7890\n\n### Step 2: Fix Desktop App\n\nThe Claude Desktop app is an Electron app that does NOT read `~/.zshrc`. Two approaches:\n\nOption A: Launch with proxy env vars (quick test)\n    \n    open -a \"Claude\" --env https_proxy=http://127.0.0.1:7890 --env http_proxy=http://127.0.0.1:7890\n\nOption B: Set system-level env vars (permanent)\n    \n    launchctl setenv https_proxy http://127.0.0.1:7890\n    launchctl setenv http_proxy http://127.0.0.1:7890\n    launchctl setenv all_proxy socks5://127.0.0.1:7890\n\nThen launch Claude Desktop normally. Note: `launchctl setenv` does not persist across reboots. ## Codex progress · 2026-07-31T14:12:22.962Z

The plan will use OmniHarness’s existing interactive terminal transport for Claude’s official login flow. That gives local and remote runners the same complete experience: the browser can open normally, and SSH/headless users can copy the shown URL and paste the authorization code back into the same authenticated terminal. Raw OAuth output remains memory-only and is never written to account records or events.

Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.\n+\n+**Goal:** Let a user connect, verify, select, inspect, log out, unregister, and explicitly purge multiple isolated Claude Code subscription accounts from OmniHarness without exposing credentials or allowing ambient Anthropic environment variables to override the selected account.\n+\n+**Architecture:** Keep the existing `accounts` table, allocator, run preference, and account-aware worker pool as the source of truth. Add a Claude-specific server service that launches the official `claude auth` commands inside a server-computed `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, using the existing authenticated PTY/SSE terminal transport for browser and headless/SSH login. Persist coarse account lifecycle state on the account row, keep OAuth terminal output and process handles memory-only, reconcile interrupted logins on runner startup, and expose every decision through typed named events.\n+\n+**Tech Stack:** TypeScript, Node.js child processes and `node-pty`, Drizzle/SQLite, Fetch-compatible runtime routes, SSE, React 19 Manager classes, existing shadcn/Base UI primitives, xterm.js, Vitest, lifecycle HTTP/SSE scenarios, Playwright for deterministic UI coverage.\n+\n+**North Star Product:** OmniHarness offers first-class, trustworthy account management for every coding CLI: connect through the provider's official flow, see real identity and health, choose an account or automatic policy per run, understand quota and failures, and manage local credential data without OmniHarness ever reading or persisting tokens.\n+\n+**Current Milestone:** Deliver the complete Claude Code subscription-account lifecycle for local and remote runners, including isolated login, real status verification, safe worker launch, reconnect/cancel behavior, logout, unregister-with-data-preserved, explicit purge, UI status, and control-plane coverage.\n+\n+**Future Product Direction:** Apply the same provider-adapter contract to Codex, Gemini, and OpenCode after the Claude implementation proves the lifecycle. This context is not part of the checklist below.\n+\n+**Final Functionality Standard:** A user can complete the entire Claude subscription-account journey from OmniHarness on desktop or mobile-sized UI, including headless/SSH authorization-code entry, and deterministic tests prove that the correct isolated account—not an ambient API key, gateway, local session, or another profile—is used. No fake login screen, copied token, hidden terminal state, or silent failure qualifies as completion.\n+\n+---\n+\n+## Approved product decisions\n+\n+- OmniHarness will integrate the official `claude auth login/status/logout` commands; it will not vendor, shell through, or depend on `claude-account`.\n+- Each additional Claude subscription account uses an OmniHarness-owned directory under `app-data/account-cli-homes/claude/<accountId>/config`, selected with `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`.\n+- The account row is created disabled before login so the operation has a durable subject. It becomes enabled only after a successful status verification and onboarding finalization.\n+- Official Claude Code owns credential creation, storage, refresh, and revocation. OmniHarness stores only the directory pointer and safe identity/status metadata.\n+- The login UI uses the real CLI in an authenticated terminal. This preserves Claude Code's browser flow and its authorization-code fallback for SSH, containers, and remote runners.\n+- Disable, log out, unregister, and purge remain separate actions:\n+  - **Disable** blocks new allocations and leaves the active credential and files untouched.\n+  - **Log out** runs official Claude logout, keeps the account row and non-credential profile data, and marks the account as requiring login.\n+  - **Remove from OmniHarness** removes the inventory record and dependent account records but preserves the profile directory.\n+  - **Purge local data** is an explicit destructive action that removes the inventory record and the exact server-owned profile directory after a second confirmation.\n+- Logout, unregister, and purge are refused while a non-terminal worker is allocated to the account. Disable remains available because it affects only new allocations.\n+- Existing worker processes are never switched to a different account. New workers and prewarmed workers receive the selected account's exact environment and account-aware pool key.\n+- The implementation works in the current checkout. It must not create a branch or worktree.\n+\n+## User stories and acceptance criteria\n+\n+1. **Connect:** As a user, I can name a second Claude account, optionally prefill an email or require SSO, complete Claude's official login, and see the verified email/subscription type before using it.\n+2. **Headless/remote:** As a user connected to a remote runner, I can copy the URL printed by Claude and paste the returned authorization code into the same terminal.\n+3. **Return/revisit:** If I close and reopen settings while the runner remains alive, I can reattach to the login terminal. If the runner restarted, the account shows an interrupted/login-required state and offers Retry rather than pretending login is still running.\n+4. **Selection safety:** When I select an isolated Claude account, ambient Anthropic API keys, auth tokens, OAuth tokens, base URLs, and the macOS global-keychain bridge cannot override it.\n+5. **Status:** Refresh performs a real account-scoped `claude auth status --json` probe and updates safe identity/status metadata. The client cannot submit an arbitrary status value.\n+6. **Failure/recovery:** Missing Claude binaries, nonzero login exits, malformed status JSON, timeouts, cancellation, onboarding-write failure, cross-profile credential bleed, and runner restart all produce an accurate visible state plus named events and `error.surfaced` where user action is needed.\n+7. **Manage:** I can disable, retry login, log out, unregister without deleting files, or explicitly purge local data, with active-worker protection and clear destructive confirmation.\n+8. **Privacy:** Account DTOs, snapshots, events, logs, SQLite, and tests never contain credential contents, authorization codes, terminal output, or OAuth URLs.\n+\n+## File map\n+\n+### Files to create\n+\n+- `src/server/accounts/cli-home.ts` — single server-owned resolver for account CLI-home roots and Claude config paths;
